idea: Accessibility of zone i: a_i = sum_j d_j * exp(-beta * t_ij) (Eq 3.2, A.1; beta 0.10, 0.13 default, 0.16 for work travel in a small region; 0.14 in the Alamo study) where d_j are destinations (jobs) and t_ij peak-hour auto time; regional accessibility = population-weighted sum (Eq 3.3: A = sum_i a_i h_i). Simpler cumulative-opportunities score counts destinations reachable within T minutes (15/30/45). Utility (logsum) scores are the third family. Use one consistent beta when comparing regions; report population-weighted average and the distribution by percentile (10th and 90th resident) rather than only the map.
does: Compute for each junction/boundary end or institution catchment the number of jobs, schools, hospitals, shops (institution employees, people) reachable within T minutes and the gravity score with a chosen beta, by mode (car, bus, walk) using run travel times or free-flow routes; population-weighted mean, percentiles, and a map layer.
inputs: mode, T minutes or beta, destination kind, time basis (free flow or a run's link times)
outputs: per-origin accessibility table, population-weighted mean, percentiles, map overlay
existing: partial: list_institutions (catchments, people, employees), institution_mode_split (route km, utilities), network_indices (graph indices); no opportunity-reach metric
cite: Ch 3 Approaches to Measuring Accessibility, Eq 3.2-3.3; Ch 4; Appendix A Step 1, Eq A.1
notes: Gives ACMS a design objective other than delay: how many opportunities people can reach. Impedance exp(-beta t) is a deterrence function already in the gravity demand model; reuse its fitted beta.

topic: Accessibility elasticity for a development or road project
idea: Accessibility elasticity = [(access_after - access_before)/access_before] / [(pop_after - pop_before)/pop_before] (Eq 3.1, A.3), computed with total (not average) regional accessibility; 1.0 means the marginal person or job contributes like the average; above 1.0 improves average accessibility. Procedure: (1) total regional accessibility; (2) traffic impact analysis gives added delay at nearby intersections; (3) route every zone pair and add the delay to routes crossing those intersections, re-routing if the fastest route changes; (4) add population or jobs to the zone (units x household size; one retail job per 47 m2); (5) recompute and take elasticity. Results 0.59, 1.86, 1.49 for three Ann Arbor developments.
does: For a proposed institution or housing block, run the traffic impact in ACMS (paired runs with and without its trips), update zone-to-zone times from the run's link delays, recompute gravity accessibility, and return the elasticity and a verdict versus 1.0.
inputs: institution to add (kind, area, people, employees), beta, run duration, seeds
outputs: accessibility before/after, change in regional size, elasticity, delay added at nearby junctions
existing: partial: place_institution, deploy_institutions, run_experiment; not built: a what-if cannot add a building's trips (docs not_built)
cite: Ch 3 Evaluating the Accessibility of Land-Use Developments, Eq 3.1, Appendix A Steps 1-5, Table 3.1
notes: Needs the institution trip generation in a scenario (known gap). The 47 m2 per retail job conversion is a US planning figure.

topic: Mobility vs accessibility comparison with speed-only counterfactual
idea: Compare build and no-build by both mobility (aggregate travel time T = sum_ij f_ij t_ij, Eq 3.4; average trip time) and accessibility; add a speed-only scenario that applies the new travel times to the old land use, separating the speed effect from the land-use (proximity) effect; scenario results show faster roads can raise mobility yet lower accessibility if destinations move farther.
does: For an experiment, report each scenario's total vehicle-minutes and mean trip time next to its accessibility, plus the share of accessibility change due to speed with institutions fixed.
outputs: table: aggregate travel time, mean trip time, accessibility, change vs baseline, speed-only effect
cite: Ch 3 Evaluating the Accessibility of Transportation Projects, Eq 3.4, Table 3.2
notes: In ACMS land use is fixed per experiment, so the speed-only effect is the default; the report just adds accessibility.

topic: Mode-location match ratio and accessibility equity
idea: MLMR = sum_i (a_i^t s_i^t) / sum_i (a_i^a s_i^a) (Eq 6.1), transit accessibility weighted by the share of transit-dependent (carless) households in each zone over auto accessibility weighted by the share of car-owning households; usually 0 to 1, about 0.4 at best in the US; compared with the unweighted ratio of regional transit to auto accessibility; also the share of transit-dependent households in each accessibility quartile; Gini index of public-transport accessibility across the population; population percentile curve (10th, 90th).
does: Equity indicators of a design: Gini of accessibility across origins weighted by people, share of carless/walk-mode people in the top and bottom accessibility quartiles, and the mode-location match ratio of bus vs car accessibility using the institutions' mode shares.
inputs: accessibility table, population by origin, carless share
outputs: Gini, quartile shares, MLMR, unweighted ratio
existing: none (institution_mode_split gives mode shares; no distributional measure)
cite: Ch 6 Mode-Location Match Ratio, Eq 6.1; Ch 5 Gini Index
notes: ACMS has no household car ownership; use the Walk/Bus mode share of each origin's people as the dependent share.

idea: Transit accessibility must use total time: access walk, wait, boarding, in-vehicle, transfer and egress; frequency matters (a 15-minute headway is worth far more than 30), either by weighting stations by frequency or by averaging the trip time over departure times every minute in the peak; assume walking to a stop on the network with a threshold (zones beyond 2 km get zero transit accessibility); limit transfers to one or two; separate rail and bus.
does: Compute transit trip time between origin and destination as walk to stop + half the headway (or averaged over departure offsets) + in-vehicle + egress, with a walking limit, for use in accessibility and mode choice.
inputs: bus stops, headways, walk speed, walk limit
existing: partial: choose_modes (out-of-vehicle time + half headway), add_bus_stop
cite: Ch 5 Technical Challenges in Measuring Public-Transport Accessibility
notes: ACMS buses have no passenger boarding model (not built); this is a static estimate.

idea: Nonwork destinations weighted by the trips they attract: N_m = J_m (0.823/0.177) nonwork trips from jobs (Eq 7.1), split by purpose share E_r (7.2), per-job rate N_r/J_r (7.3), zone attractiveness W_i = sum_r (N_r/J_r) J_ir (7.4); hospitals included for assurance value; visiting friends attracted by population; 24 nonwork categories.
does: Use each institution kind's daily trips (already stored) as the destination weight d_j in accessibility, with hospitals given a floor weight, so a school, shop and hospital count differently.
existing: partial: institutions (people a day each way)
notes: Constants are US national shares; only the weighting principle transfers.

idea: Project prioritisation with six factor areas and 1-3 measures each, normalised to compare small and large projects: safety (fatal/injury crash count 50%, rate 50%), congestion mitigation (person throughput 50%, person-hours of delay 50%), accessibility (access to jobs 60%, to jobs for disadvantaged 20%, multimodal choices 20%), environment, economic development (reliability 20%), land use; region-specific factor weights (recommended 45% congestion, 15% accessibility in large metros).
does: Rank design alternatives from an experiment on a weighted scorecard of ACMS KPIs (person delay, person throughput, safety conflict rate, accessibility, reliability PTI), with weights the user sets, per-cost normalisation and a sensitivity check of the ranking to the weights.
outputs: ranked alternatives with factor scores and weight sensitivity
existing: partial: compare_runs, analyse_safety, analyse_run (PTI), people carried in results
notes: Pairs with accessibility_analysis; the weighting scheme is policy, not a model, so the weights stay user inputs.
